modules.name: minisvc.cli
modules.purpose: CLI bootstrap: loads settings, constructs the repository, initializes the SQLite schema, and prints readiness.

modules.name: minisvc.config
modules.purpose: Defines Settings and translates environment variables into runtime configuration.

modules.name: minisvc.models
modules.purpose: Defines the Order dataclass shared between handlers, repository, and audit helpers.

modules.name: minisvc.storage.repo
modules.purpose: SQLite persistence adapter for initializing schema, inserting orders, and fetching orders by id.

modules.name: minisvc.audit
modules.purpose: Builds lightweight in-memory audit event dictionaries returned in handler responses; does not persist them.

modules.name: minisvc.api.handlers
modules.purpose: Implements create/read order use cases, mapping payloads to Order objects and repository calls.

modules.name: minisvc.api.routes
modules.purpose: Registers HTTP route callbacks that delegate to the order handlers.

modules.name: minisvc.__init__
modules.purpose: Package marker exporting config and models; not active business logic.

modules.name: minisvc.api.__init__
modules.purpose: Package marker only; no business logic.

modules.name: minisvc.storage.__init__
modules.purpose: Package marker only; no business logic.

entry_points.evidence: registers POST /orders and GET /orders/<order_id> handlers onto an app object

dependency_edges.to: sqlite database orders.sqlite or MINISVC_DB target

key_functions.summary: Application bootstrap that loads config from os.environ, creates OrderRepository, initializes the orders table, and returns exit code 0.
key_functions.notes: Only startup path that ensures schema creation.

key_functions.summary: Builds a frozen Settings object from MINISVC_DB and MINISVC_READONLY environment variables.
key_functions.notes: readonly is parsed but not enforced elsewhere in the codebase.

key_functions.summary: Creates the orders SQLite table if it does not already exist.
key_functions.notes: No audit table or migrations are created.

key_functions.summary: Inserts an Order row into SQLite using a fresh connection per call.
key_functions.notes: No retry, no upsert, and IntegrityError bubbles to caller on duplicate order_id.

key_functions.summary: Reads one order row from SQLite and rehydrates it into an Order dataclass.
key_functions.notes: Returns None when the row is absent.

key_functions.summary: Maps incoming payload fields to an Order, saves it, and returns a created response with an embedded audit event dict.
key_functions.notes: Uses direct dict indexing and int conversion; malformed payloads raise KeyError/ValueError.

key_functions.summary: Fetches an order by id and returns either a missing response or an ok response containing the order and an audit event dict.
key_functions.notes: Audit event is generated on read but not persisted.

key_functions.summary: Attaches POST and GET route lambdas to the provided app object.
key_functions.notes: Assumes app exposes post and get methods; no framework-specific types are declared.

key_functions.summary: Builds an audit/event dictionary from an Order and action string.
key_functions.notes: Pure function only; no storage side effects.

runtime_flows.name: CLI startup flow
steps: pyproject.toml exposes the minisvc console script pointing to minisvc.cli:main.
load_settings resolves MINISVC_DB (default orders.sqlite) and MINISVC_READONLY (default false).
main instantiates minisvc.storage.repo.OrderRepository with the configured database path.
main calls repo.init_schema() to create the orders table if needed.
main prints a readiness message and exits with status code 0.

runtime_flows.name: HTTP create-order flow
steps: A hosting layer calls minisvc.api.routes.register_routes(app, repo).
register_routes wires POST /orders to minisvc.api.handlers.create_order via a lambda that closes over repo.
create_order pulls order_id, customer, and total_cents directly from the payload and constructs minisvc.models.Order.
create_order calls OrderRepository.save(order), which opens SQLite and inserts into the orders table.
create_order calls minisvc.audit.order_event(order, "created") to build a response-side event dict.
The handler returns {status: "created", order_id, event}; exceptions from validation or SQLite propagate because there is no local error handling or retry.

runtime_flows.name: HTTP read-order flow
steps: GET /orders/<order_id> is wired to minisvc.api.handlers.get_order by register_routes.
Repository performs a SELECT and returns either an Order instance or None.
Handler returns {status: "missing"} when absent, otherwise returns the order payload plus an in-memory audit event.
